question: Can a package cause code to run during install, update or uninstall - through a lifecycle script, a postinstall hook, an auto-loaded config or a build step - and is that execution sandboxed or refused?
title: Install-time script execution policy for packages

reviewer.notes: Probe 2 re-derives invocation points from AST of pipeline sources and a live subprocess.run trace, not from probe 1's beacon table or from a prose summary of this report.

method.probe1: Probe 1: install the fixture in a sandbox and check for the beacon written by each vector.
method.probe2: Probe 2 (mechanically different): read the pipeline source to enumerate every point where an external command could be invoked, then confirm the fixture actually exercised each - an unexercised vector is NOT-CHECKED, not safe.
method.declared_policy: scripts.postinstall is not implicit; sandbox requires owner gate

targets.claim: Plugin helpers on this tree honour a package-declared lifecycle script and execute it during install/update/uninstall.
A plugin-shaped package with scripts.postinstall runs that script on the default marketplace install path.
sitecustomize.py / plugin.json planted in the payload is imported or executed during install without an explicit script field.
scripts.build is invoked by the marketplace installer.
An uninstall pipeline honours scripts.uninstall and runs it.
Marketplace install executes package payload code on the default (no owner gate) path.
A package can cause subprocess.run of its postinstall script when the owner gate plus sandbox is granted, or via the naive host control.
When the installer does run a package script on the owner-gated path, the beacon stays inside the sandbox and host-marker env is stripped.
A Claude/Cursor host automatically executes plugin hook commands declared in copied hook JSON.
